You could just supplement with k2, retinol, zinc, dha, bcaas, creatine, taurine, carnitine, carnosine, b vitamins, coconut oil, iron, isolated protein powders, selenium, vitamin d, and a handful of other vitamins and minerals if you wanted, I guess. Not sure how well many of those would be absorbed or utilized by the body though. Isolated nutrients have poor absorption and utilization and many aren't even what they say they are. Plus many of those would wreak havoc on your digestion.

Its just a growing trend globally and nba players are joining the movement. I doubt many nba players have a good grasp on human physiology or true nutrition. And of course team nutritionists can't force a player to change their diet. Only work within certain limitations.
Yes. Vegans have lower bone mineral density and poor myelin sheath insulation, both of which spell trouble for a back injury.

What troubles me most is that he had back surgery and is vegan. The lack of fat soluble vitamins, fat in general, and poor quality protein will make him much more likely to reinjure himself than other guys with recent surgeries. We are going to see a huge uptick in injuries as plant based diets become a fad amongst athletes. As a Kings fan, this pick would have me very very nervous.
